hints: The edges needed to visit all coins form a minimal connecting subtree.
In a tree, edges outside the direct start-to-end path must be traversed twice.
Add both endpoints to the coin subtree, accounting for any shared part of their branches.
analogy: Draw the smallest connected network containing every coin and both endpoints. Every side branch needs an out-and-back trip.
example: If the required subtree has 3 edges and the start-to-end path has 1 edge, the shortest walk has length 2*3-1=5.
algorithm: Prune coin-free leaves to find the minimal coin subtree S and its edge count E. Multi-source BFS from S gives d(v), distance to S. Preprocess LCA for tree distances. For query a,b let overlap=max(0,(d(a)+d(b)-dist(a,b))/2). The union of S and the two paths from a and b to S has E+d(a)+d(b)-overlap edges. Return twice this number minus dist(a,b).
correctness: The two paths to S overlap exactly when the endpoints join the same branch before reaching S, and the distance identity gives the shared length. Every edge of the resulting minimal subtree is needed; its start-to-end path is traversed once and all other edges twice. A depth-first walk attains this bound.
complexity: For n vertices and q queries, preprocessing takes O(n log n) time and space; each query takes O(log n).
